thread:
Anna (Docs): Quick heads-up 1: we need a lightweight spec for glossary canonical IDs + example casing for the Q2 docs sweep. Spotted mixed param names in snippets across guides. Can someone volunteer to own a tiny checklist?

Kiran (PM): Happy to own the checklist. Keep it short: canonical_id, display_name, canonical_example, aliases. We should also capture language mappings (py/js).

Diego (SDK): I'll handle snippet updates once the mapping file exists. Planning a small token-replace script that runs as part of docs CI.

Matt R: Re PRs: there are a few open PRs touching snippets. I'll open a gating PR that adds docs/data/canonical_map.yaml so other PRs can reference it and avoid merge conflicts.

Anna (Docs): Love it. Can the gating PR also enable link-check + snippet-compile so we catch broken references early?

link-bot: Found 2 broken links in docs/guides/migrate-paramcase.md -> /api/paramcase (404)

Diego (SDK): I'll prepare update_snippets.py and a unit test to validate snippet placeholders compile. Suggest placeholder format [[CANON:param_timeout]] so replacements are deterministic.

Kiran (PM): Small decision needed: docs canonical examples use snake_case (python-first) OR language-neutral names? Which is preferred?

Anna (Docs): Decision: use snake_case for the canonical example in prose and code blocks labelled Python. For JS blocks, include an explicit mapped example and a one-line note above the snippet describing the mapping. Example to include in the checklist:
```python
# canonical docs example (python)
client.create(request, timeout_seconds=30)
```
```javascript
// mapped JS example
client.create(request, timeoutSeconds: 30)
```
Add a short comment above each code block saying: "Param names shown in Python snake_case; JS mapping: camelCase."

Matt R: I'll add the gating PR and include a small grep run to find "paramCase"/"param-case"/"param_case" variants and post results so we can alias them.

Diego (SDK): Will the canonical_map.yaml include entries like: canonical_id: param_timeout, aliases: ["timeoutSeconds","timeout_seconds","timeout-seconds"], lang_map: {py: "timeout_seconds", js: "timeoutSeconds"}?

Anna (Docs): Keep the YAML flat for now. We can't include nested objects in some of our tooling. Use keys like: id, display_name, py_example, js_example, aliases (comma-separated). Kiran, put that format in the checklist.

link-bot: gating PR #610 created by Matt R. CI: link-check queued.

Kiran (PM): I'll draft the one-page checklist and a tiny sample table and drop it here by EOD. We want writers to: 1) reference canonical_map.yaml, 2) use placeholder tokens in new snippets, 3) add a language-mapping note.

Matt R: Will set PR to require link-check + snippets compile. Please don't merge snippet changes until mapping lands.

Diego (SDK): Quick ask: should tests enforce that every placeholder has a mapping? I can add a fail-fast check in snippet-compile if a placeholder isn't in canonical_map.yaml.

Anna (Docs): Yes, fail-fast. Also add a docs-lint rule to flag free-form param variants in prose (simple grep).

Kiran (PM): Filed issue #4890 to track the migration and included initial alias list.

Anna (Docs): Great work team. Final summary: Kiran -> checklist + sample table; Matt -> gating PR w/ canonical_map.yaml + grep; Diego -> snippet updater + compile tests; Anna -> docs-lint rule proposal. We'll reconvene if CI flags anything. :thumbsup:

link-bot: gating PR #610 link-check passed; snippet-compile passed. All green.
